picks.title: How to take over a design built in Figma Make and develop it with Claude Code
picks.excerpt: Four apps started from Figma Make code bundles; the author traces via config files and commit history how far each got once development continued in Claude Code, and where they stalled.
picks.rationale: Concrete, reproducible handoff evidence from Figma Make output to Claude Code - directly changes how a designer plans a build.

picks.title: I saw NVIDIA's new AI video tool: why RTX Spark's half-frame trick might actually matter
picks.excerpt: Generate half the frames and let local RTX Spark AI infer the rest: a Full HD two-second clip drops from about 6m30s to about 1m25s, with offline interpolation avoiding real-time frame-gen artefacts.
picks.rationale: Hands-on demo with hard timings; changes the economics of iterating on AI video.

picks.title: AI in Product teams: In 2026, the growing impact on collaboration
picks.excerpt: Companies with top-down AI mandates see the biggest gains; 56% of non-designers now do design work, 65% of designers take on product or engineering work, and team sizes may shrink from 8-10 to 2-3.
picks.rationale: Numbers a design org can act on when planning its own AI adoption structure.

picks.title: DESIGN.md - a shared UI design guide for working with AI
picks.excerpt: Google Labs frames DESIGN.md as a persistent structured way to hand a design system to an AI agent: machine-readable tokens in YAML front matter, human-readable intent in the markdown body. Status is alpha.
picks.rationale: An immediately adoptable artifact for keeping agent output on-brand.

picks.title: This AI Turns Insane Ideas Into 3D Objects
picks.excerpt: Tripo 2.0 turns almost any image into a full 3D model you can export to Blender, Unreal Engine or a 3D printer.
picks.rationale: Image-to-3D that lands as an exportable asset - a real step for product and concept designers.
